question: After the fall of the Guptas, different kingdoms emerged in various parts of India. Among them, the Maukharis emerged in which of the following areas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kannauj.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Maukhari dynasty emerged in the Kannauj (Kanyakubja) region of present-day Uttar Pradesh after the decline of the Gupta Empire in the 6th century CE. (मौखरि वंश — कन्नौज)

 

• The Maukharis were initially feudatories of the Guptas but became independent and made Kannauj their capital, ruling over the region roughly corresponding to modern-day western Uttar Pradesh.

 

• Their most notable ruler was Ishanavarman, who assumed the title of Maharajadhiraja; the dynasty's power later merged into Harshavardhana's empire through matrimonial alliance (Harsha's sister Rajyashri was married to the Maukhari king Grahavarman).

 

• Kannauj subsequently became one of the most important political centres of early medieval North India, contested by the Pratiharas, Palas and Rashtrakutas in the "Tripartite Struggle".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Thanesar (Sthanvishvara) was the capital of the Pushyabhuti (Vardhana) dynasty, including Harshavardhana, before he shifted his capital to Kannauj.

 

• Valabhi in Gujarat was the capital of the Maitraka dynasty, another post-Gupta successor state.

 

NOTE

 

• Thanesar (Option 1): This was the capital of the Pushyabhuti dynasty, not the Maukharis.

 

• Kunnur (Option 2): Not associated with any major post-Gupta kingdom; it is a town in South India, unrelated to the Maukharis.

 

• Valabhi (Option 3): This was the capital of the Maitraka dynasty in Gujarat, not the Maukharis.

question: Which of the following nations won the ICC World Test Championship, defeating India, in 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Australia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Australia defeated India by 209 runs in the final of the 2021-2023 ICC World Test Championship (WTC), held at The Oval, London, in June 2023. (विश्व टेस्ट चैंपियनशिप — ऑस्ट्रेलिया)

 

• This was the second edition of the WTC; the first edition (2019-2021) was won by New Zealand, who defeated India in the final at Southampton in 2021.

 

• Travis Head was named Player of the Match for his century in the 2023 final, and Pat Cummins captained the winning Australian side.

 

• With this win, Australia later completed a rare "double" by also winning the 2023 ODI World Cup final, again against India, in Ahmedabad.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The WTC final venues for both the 2021 and 2023 editions were in England (Southampton and The Oval respectively).

 

• The third WTC cycle (2023-2025) final was won by South Africa, who defeated Australia at Lord's in June 2025.

 

NOTE

 

• New Zealand (Option 1): They won the first WTC final in 2021, defeating India, not the 2023 one.

 

• South Africa (Option 3): They won the third WTC final in 2025, defeating Australia — they did not contest the 2023 final.

 

• England (Option 4): England has not contested a WTC final so far.

question: Presently, which of the following countries is NOT a beneficiary of India's Duty-Free Tariff Preference (DFTP) Scheme?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Angola.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's Duty-Free Tariff Preference (DFTP) Scheme, launched in 2008, grants preferential/duty-free market access to India for products from notified Least Developed Countries (LDCs). Angola is not among the notified beneficiary countries under this scheme. (शुल्क-मुक्त शुल्क वरीयता योजना — अंगोला लाभार्थी नहीं)

 

• The scheme presently covers around 33 LDCs across Africa, Asia and the Pacific, granting preferential access on tariff lines comprising a very large share of world tariff lines.

 

• Rwanda, Burundi and Myanmar are all notified beneficiaries of the DFTP scheme.

 

• The scheme is administered by India's Ministry of Commerce and Industry and aims to boost trade with, and development of, LDCs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other DFTP beneficiaries include Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Ethiopia, Haiti, Lesotho, Madagascar, Malawi, Mozambique, Senegal, Tanzania, Uganda, Yemen and Zambia, among others.

 

NOTE

 

• Rwanda (Option 1): It is a notified beneficiary of the DFTP scheme.

 

• Burundi (Option 2): It is a notified beneficiary of the DFTP scheme.

 

• Myanmar (Option 3): It is a notified beneficiary of the DFTP scheme.

question: Which of the following Articles deals with the composition of the Rajya Sabha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 80.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 80 of the Indian Constitution deals with the composition of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States). (राज्यसभा की संरचना — अनुच्छेद 80)

 

• The Rajya Sabha can have a maximum of 250 members — 12 members nominated by the President (persons with special knowledge/practical experience in literature, science, art and social service) and not more than 238 representatives of the States and Union Territories, elected indirectly.

 

• Members representing states are elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies through the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.

 

• The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and is not subject to dissolution; one-third of its members retire every second year, as provided under Article 83.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 79 establishes the Parliament of India, consisting of the President, the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha.

 

• Article 81 deals with the composition of the Lok Sabha.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 76 (Option 1): This deals with the Attorney General of India.

 

• Article 84 (Option 3): This lays down the qualifications for membership of Parliament.

 

• Article 92 (Option 4): This deals with restrictions on discussion in the Rajya Sabha regarding the conduct of its Chairman/Deputy Chairman while a resolution for their removal is under consideration.

question: The birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi is celebrated as the national festival of India. In which of the following years was Gandhi ji born?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1869.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mahatma Gandhi was born on 2 October 1869 in Porbandar, Gujarat. His birth anniversary, Gandhi Jayanti, is celebrated as a national festival every year on 2 October. (गांधी जयंती — 2 अक्टूबर 1869)

 

• 2 October is also observed globally as the International Day of Non-Violence, declared by the United Nations General Assembly in 2007, in honour of Gandhi's philosophy of Ahimsa (non-violence).

 

• India observes only three national festivals: Republic Day (26 January), Independence Day (15 August), and Gandhi Jayanti (2 October).

 

• Gandhi is popularly known as the "Father of the Nation" and led India's freedom struggle through movements like the Non-Cooperation Movement, Civil Disobedience Movement, and Quit India Movement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gandhi was assassinated on 30 January 1948 by Nathuram Godse; this day is observed as Martyrs' Day (Shaheed Diwas) in India.

 

NOTE

 

• 1885 (Option 1): This is the year the Indian National Congress was founded, not Gandhi's birth year.

 

• 1890 (Option 3): Not the correct year of Gandhi's birth.

 

• 1877 (Option 4): Not the correct year of Gandhi's birth.

question: What kind of phyllotaxy was examined in the Guava plant?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Opposite.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Phyllotaxy refers to the pattern/arrangement of leaves on a plant stem. The Guava (Psidium guajava) plant exhibits opposite (opposite-decussate) phyllotaxy. (पत्ती विन्यास — अमरूद में सम्मुख विन्यास)

 

• In opposite phyllotaxy, two leaves arise at each node, situated opposite to each other; in the decussate form (as in guava), each successive pair is set at right angles to the pair below it, as also seen in plants like Calotropis and Ixora.

 

• The main types of phyllotaxy are alternate (e.g., China rose, mustard), opposite (e.g., guava, Calotropis), whorled (e.g., Alstonia, Nerium), and opposite superimposed (e.g., Quisqualis).

 

• Phyllotaxy patterns help maximise exposure of leaves to sunlight for efficient photosynthesis and minimise overlapping/shading between leaves.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Whorled phyllotaxy, where more than two leaves arise at a single node forming a whorl, is seen in plants like Alstonia (Devil's tree) and Nerium (oleander).

 

NOTE

 

• Superimposed (Option 1): This refers to opposite superimposed phyllotaxy, seen in plants like Quisqualis (Rangoon creeper), not guava.

 

• Whorled (Option 2): Seen in plants such as Alstonia and Nerium, where more than two leaves emerge from a single node.

 

• Alternate (Option 3): Seen in plants such as China rose (Hibiscus), mustard and sunflower, where a single leaf arises at each node.

question: The Nandi Award for Best Male Playback Singer was instituted by which state in the year 1977?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Nandi Awards are film awards presented annually by the Government of Andhra Pradesh for excellence in Telugu cinema; the Best Male Playback Singer category was instituted in 1977. (नंदी पुरस्कार — आंध्र प्रदेश)

 

• The awards are named after the Nandi (the sacred bull, Lord Shiva's mount), reflecting stone Nandi statues at temples such as Lepakshi.

 

• The Nandi Awards are considered one of the oldest state-level film honours in India, first instituted in 1964.

 

• Winners typically receive gold, silver and bronze Nandi statuettes across various categories.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Similar state-level film awards include the Kalaimamani Award (Tamil Nadu) and Filmfare Awards South, which honour films across South Indian languages.

 

NOTE

 

• Gujarat (Option 1): Does not institute the Nandi Awards; Gujarat has its own separate state film awards.

 

• Tripura (Option 3): Not associated with the Nandi Awards.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 4): Maharashtra's state film honours include the Maharashtra State Film Awards, distinct from the Nandi Awards.

question: Indian Olympic Association was established in which of the following years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1927.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) was established in 1927 to promote the Olympic Movement in India and to organise the country's participation in the Olympic Games. (भारतीय ओलंपिक संघ — 1927)

 

• Sir Dorabji Tata is widely credited as a founding figure associated with organising early Indian participation in the Olympics, and Dr. A.G. Noehren served as the first president of the IOA.

 

• The IOA is headquartered in New Delhi and is responsible for selecting athletes to represent India at the Olympic Games, Asian Games, and Commonwealth Games.

 

• India's first appearance at the Olympics (as British India) had begun informally in 1900, well before the IOA's formal establishment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India made its official Olympic debut with a formal contingent in 1920 at the Antwerp Olympics, before the IOA was formally established.

 

NOTE

 

• 1931, 1933, 1929 (Options 2, 3, 4): None of these correspond to the year the IOA was established; the correct year is 1927.

question: Which of the following is a public sector industry?
solution_text:
The correct answer is BHEL.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• BHEL (Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited) is a public sector undertaking (PSU), owned by the Government of India, under the Ministry of Heavy Industries. (सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र उद्योग — भेल)

 

• BHEL was established in 1964 and is one of India's largest engineering and manufacturing companies, producing power plant and other industrial equipment.

 

• BHEL holds the status of a Maharatna Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE), a category granted to select large, well-performing PSUs.

 

• Public sector industries are wholly or majority owned by the government, in contrast to private sector companies, which are owned by private individuals or entities.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major Maharatna PSUs include ONGC, NTPC, Coal India, SAIL, and Indian Oil Corporation.

 

NOTE

 

• Reliance (Option 2): A privately owned Indian conglomerate, led by the Ambani family.

 

• Tata (Option 3): A privately owned Indian conglomerate group (Tata Sons).

 

• Adani (Option 4): A privately owned Indian conglomerate, led by the Adani family.

question: Which of following is NOT a device of parliamentary proceedings?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Full-day discussion.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Full-day discussion" is not a recognised parliamentary device in the Indian Parliament; standard devices for raising matters include Zero Hour, Question Hour, Half-an-Hour Discussion, Short Duration (two-hour) Discussion, Calling Attention, and various motions. (संसदीय प्रक्रिया के साधन — पूर्ण-दिवस चर्चा मान्य नहीं)

 

• Half-an-Hour Discussion is used to discuss a matter of sufficient public importance that has been the subject of a recent question in the House and the answer to which needs elucidation.

 

• Zero Hour is an Indian parliamentary innovation (not mentioned in the Rules of Procedure) that starts immediately after Question Hour, around 12 noon, allowing members to raise urgent matters without prior notice.

 

• Short Duration (Two-hour) Discussion allows members to raise discussion on a matter of urgent public importance without a formal motion or voting.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important parliamentary devices include Calling Attention Motion, Adjournment Motion, No-Confidence Motion, and Censure Motion.

 

NOTE

 

• Half-an-hour discussion (Option 1): This is a recognised device of parliamentary proceedings.

 

• Zero-hour discussion (Option 2): This is a recognised (though procedurally informal) device of parliamentary proceedings.

 

• Two-hour (short) discussion (Option 3): This is a recognised device of parliamentary proceedings, formally called the Short Duration Discussion.

question: Which of the following rivers marks the eastern-most boundary of the Himalayas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brahmaputra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Himalayas extend from the Indus River in the west to the Brahmaputra River in the east, a stretch of about 2,500 km. (हिमालय की पूर्वी सीमा — ब्रह्मपुत्र नदी)

 

• The eastern extremity of the Himalayas is marked by the great bend of the Brahmaputra River around Namcha Barwa peak, after which the range turns south into the Purvanchal (Eastern) hills.

 

• The Himalayas are conventionally divided (west to east) into the Punjab Himalayas, Kumaon Himalayas, Nepal Himalayas, and Assam Himalayas.

 

• The western boundary of the Himalayas is generally marked by the Indus River, near the Nanga Parbat syntaxial bend.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Himalayan range is broadly classified longitudinally into Trans-Himalayas, Greater Himalayas (Himadri), Lesser Himalayas (Himachal), and Outer Himalayas (Shiwaliks).

 

NOTE

 

• Kali (Option 1): A river forming part of the India-Nepal border, not the eastern boundary of the Himalayas.

 

• Teesta (Option 2): A major river of Sikkim and North Bengal, a tributary of the Brahmaputra, but not the eastern boundary marker.

 

• Satluj (Option 3): One of the five rivers of Punjab, flowing through the western Himalayas, not the eastern boundary.

question: What is the empirically fitted relationship between the rate of change of money, wage, and rate of unemployment known as?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Philips curve.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Phillips Curve, proposed by economist A.W. Phillips in 1958, represents the empirically observed inverse relationship between the rate of change of money wages (or inflation) and the rate of unemployment. (फिलिप्स वक्र — मजदूरी परिवर्तन दर और बेरोजगारी दर)

 

• Phillips based his original curve on data from the UK economy between 1861 and 1957, showing that periods of low unemployment tended to be associated with higher wage inflation, and vice versa.

 

• The curve implies a short-run trade-off between inflation and unemployment, which policymakers can theoretically use for macroeconomic management.

 

• Later economists like Milton Friedman and Edmund Phelps argued that in the long run, the Phillips Curve trade-off does not hold, leading to the concept of the "natural rate of unemployment".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The "Expectations-Augmented Phillips Curve", developed by Friedman and Phelps, incorporates inflationary expectations into the original model.

 

NOTE

 

• Friedman's model (Option 1): Milton Friedman contributed the concept of the natural rate of unemployment and critiqued the original Phillips Curve, but did not originate this specific empirical relationship.

 

• Keynesian model (Option 2): Refers broadly to Keynesian economics, centred on aggregate demand, not this specific wage-unemployment relationship.

 

• Baumol hypothesis (Option 3): Refers to work such as William Baumol's inventory-theoretic approach to money demand or his cost-disease hypothesis, unrelated to this relationship.

question: Which of the following is India's national academy of dance?
option_2: Centre for Cultural Resources and Training
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sangeet Natak Akademi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, established in 1952, is India's national academy for music, dance and drama, and is the oldest of the national akademis for the arts set up by the Government of India. (संगीत नाटक अकादमी — भारत की राष्ट्रीय नृत्य अकादमी)

 

• It is headquartered in New Delhi and functions under the Ministry of Culture, promoting and preserving India's heritage of performing arts, including its eight classical dance forms.

 

• The Akademi confers the prestigious Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Akademi Puraskar) and Akademi Fellowship (Ratna Sadasya), among the highest recognitions for performing artists in India.

 

• It is one of the three national akademis for arts and letters set up by the Government of India, alongside the Sahitya Akademi (literature) and Lalit Kala Akademi (visual arts).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India recognises eight classical dance forms: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, and Sattriya.

 

NOTE

 

• Lalit Kala Akademi (Option 1): India's national academy for visual arts (painting, sculpture, graphics), not dance.

 

• Centre for Cultural Resources and Training (Option 2): An autonomous organisation under the Ministry of Culture that links education with culture, but is not the national dance academy.

 

• Centre for Indian Classical Dances (Option 3): Not the officially designated national academy for dance in India.

question: Padma Bhushan awardee, Ustad Sabri Khan played which of the following musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sarangi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Sabri Khan (1927-2015) was a celebrated Indian classical musician renowned for playing the Sarangi, a bowed string instrument. (उस्ताद साबरी खान — सारंगी वादक)

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Bhushan in 2006 by the Government of India for his contribution to Hindustani classical music, having earlier received the Padma Shri in 1992.

 

• He belonged to the Moradabad-Rampur-Sahaswan gharana of Sarangi playing and was known for popularising the instrument as a solo concert instrument, beyond its traditional accompanying role.

 

• The Sarangi is traditionally used to accompany vocal music and is considered one of the instruments closest to the human voice in Hindustani classical tradition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other noted Sarangi exponents include Ustad Bundu Khan and Pandit Ram Narayan, who is also known for elevating the Sarangi to a solo concert instrument.

 

NOTE

 

• Sarod (Option 1): A plucked string instrument; noted exponents include Ustad Ali Akbar Khan and Amjad Ali Khan.

 

• Santoor (Option 2): A trapezoid-shaped hammered string instrument, popularised by Pandit Shivkumar Sharma.

 

• Tabla (Option 3): A pair of hand drums; noted exponents include Ustad Zakir Hussain and Pandit Kishan Maharaj.

question: Transition elements are the elements that are found in Groups 3-12 of the modern periodic table, that constitute the _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is d-block.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Transition elements occupy Groups 3 to 12 of the modern periodic table and are collectively called the d-block elements, as their valence electrons progressively fill the d-orbitals. (डी-ब्लॉक तत्व — संक्रमण तत्व)

 

• There are four series of d-block elements, corresponding to the filling of 3d, 4d, 5d and 6d orbitals, spanning periods 4 to 7 of the periodic table.

 

• Transition elements characteristically show properties like variable oxidation states, formation of coloured compounds, catalytic activity, and formation of complex ions, due to the involvement of d-orbitals.

 

• Common examples of transition elements include iron (Fe), copper (Cu), zinc (Zn), and silver (Ag).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Group 12 elements (like zinc, cadmium, mercury) are sometimes debated as not being "true" transition elements since they have a fully filled d-subshell, but they are still located within the d-block.

 

NOTE

 

• s-block (Option 2): Comprises Groups 1 and 2 (alkali and alkaline earth metals), where the valence electron enters the s-orbital.

 

• p-block (Option 3): Comprises Groups 13 to 18, where the valence electron enters the p-orbital.

 

• f-block (Option 4): Comprises the Lanthanides and Actinides, placed separately at the bottom of the periodic table, where valence electrons fill the f-orbitals.

question: A small object is placed on the focus on the left side of a convex lens. Where will be the image formed?
option_1: At the centre on the right side of the lens.
option_2: At infinity on the left side of the lens.
option_3: At infinity on the right side of the lens.
option_4: At the focus on the right side of the lens.
solution_text:
The correct answer is At infinity on the right side of the lens.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• For a convex (converging) lens, when an object is placed exactly at the focus (F1) on one side, the refracted rays emerge parallel to each other on the other side, so the image is formed at infinity. (उत्तल लेंस — फोकस पर वस्तु, अनंत पर प्रतिबिंब)

 

• Since the object is placed on the left side at the focal point, and light travels from left to right through the lens, the image forms at infinity on the right side of the lens.

 

• This principle is used in devices where a parallel beam is required, such as searchlights and headlights, by placing the light source at the focus of a convex lens/mirror system.

 

• As the object moves from beyond 2F towards F, the image moves from between F and 2F towards infinity, progressively becoming larger and moving farther away.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• When the object is placed at 2F, the image forms at 2F on the other side, real, inverted, and of the same size as the object.

 

• When the object is placed between F and the optical centre, the image formed is virtual, erect, and magnified, on the same side as the object — this is the principle behind a simple magnifying glass.

 

NOTE

 

• At the centre on the right side of the lens (Option 1): No real image is formed at the optical centre itself for any object position.

 

• At infinity on the left side of the lens (Option 2): Incorrect; since light travels from left to right through the lens, a real image cannot form on the same side as the object under these conditions.

 

• At the focus on the right side of the lens (Option 4): This describes the case when the object is at infinity, not when the object is placed at the focus.

question: One of the greatest of Chola ruler Rajaraja I ruled from 985 AD to ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1014 AD.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rajaraja I (Rajaraja Chola I), one of the greatest rulers of the Chola dynasty, reigned from 985 CE to 1014 CE. (राजराज प्रथम — चोल वंश, 985-1014 ई.)

 

• He is credited with building the magnificent Brihadeeswarar Temple (Rajarajeswaram) at Thanjavur, dedicated to Lord Shiva, part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site "Great Living Chola Temples".

 

• Rajaraja I expanded the Chola Empire significantly, conquering parts of Sri Lanka, the Maldives, and the Malabar coast, and reorganised the empire's administrative and revenue systems.

 

• He was succeeded by his son Rajendra Chola I, who further expanded the empire, notably with a naval expedition to Southeast Asia (Srivijaya) and campaigns up to the Ganges, earning the title "Gangaikonda Chola".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Chola dynasty is especially known for its maritime power, temple architecture, and Chola bronze sculptures, as well as for institutionalising local self-government through village assemblies described in inscriptions like those at Uttiramerur.

 

NOTE

 

• 1015 AD, 1017 AD, 1018 AD (Options 1, 2, 4): None of these correctly mark the end of Rajaraja I's reign; he ruled until 1014 CE, after which his son Rajendra Chola I succeeded him.

question: Who asked James Rennel to prepare the map of Hindustan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Robert Clive.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• James Rennell was asked by Robert Clive to prepare a map of Hindustan; Rennell was appointed the first Surveyor General of Bengal in 1767 under Clive. (जेम्स रेनेल — रॉबर्ट क्लाइव द्वारा हिंदुस्तान का मानचित्र)

 

• Rennell's most famous work, the "Map of Hindoostan", was published in 1782, along with his "Bengal Atlas" (1779), and is considered a landmark in the mapping of the Indian subcontinent.

 

• He is often referred to as the "Father of Indian Geography" or the "Father of the Indian Survey" for his pioneering cartographic and geographical work in India.

 

• Rennell's surveys laid the foundation for later systematic mapping efforts in India, including the Great Trigonometrical Survey, launched in 1802 under William Lambton.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Robert Clive was a key figure in establishing British East India Company control in Bengal, notably after the Battle of Plassey (1757) and the Battle of Buxar (1764).

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Ripen (Option 1): This refers to Lord Ripon, a Viceroy of India known for the Resolution on Local Self-Government (1882) and the Ilbert Bill controversy, unrelated to Rennell's map.

 

• Warren Hastings (Option 2): The first Governor-General of Bengal, but it was Clive, not Hastings, who commissioned Rennell's survey.

 

• Lord Dalhousie (Option 3): Known for the Doctrine of Lapse and expanding railways/telegraph in India, unrelated to Rennell's map, and active decades after Rennell's survey.

question: Who among the following is appointed as the new Chairman of Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) in March 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Deepak Mohanty.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Deepak Mohanty was appointed as the Chairman of the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) in March 2023, succeeding Supratim Bandyopadhyay. (पीएफआरडीए अध्यक्ष — दीपक मोहंती)

 

• Deepak Mohanty is a former Executive Director of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and had earlier headed the RBI's committee on Household Financial Savings.

 

• Along with his appointment, Mamta Shankar was appointed as a Whole-Time Member (Economics) of PFRDA around the same time.

 

• PFRDA was established in 2003 and regulates the National Pension System (NPS) and pension funds in India; it is headquartered in New Delhi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• PFRDA became a statutory body under the PFRDA Act, 2013, having earlier functioned under an interim non-statutory arrangement.

 

NOTE

 

• Supratim Bandopadhyay (Option 1): He was the previous PFRDA Chairman, whom Deepak Mohanty succeeded in March 2023.

 

• Shasikanta Das (Option 2): This appears to refer to Shaktikanta Das, who was the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India, not the PFRDA chairman.

 

• Mamta Shankar (Option 3): She was appointed as a Whole-Time Member of PFRDA at the same time, not as Chairman.

question: Indian National Army was formed in which of the following countries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Singapore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj) was first formed in 1942 in Singapore, following the fall of Singapore to Japanese forces, under the initiative of Mohan Singh and Indian prisoners of war. (आजाद हिंद फौज — सिंगापुर)

 

• The INA was later revitalised and reorganised in 1943 under the leadership of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, who arrived in Singapore and took command, giving the famous slogan "Delhi Chalo".

 

• Bose also proclaimed the Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind Government) in Singapore in October 1943, with the INA as its military arm.

 

• The INA fought alongside Japanese forces in the Imphal and Kohima campaigns (1944) in an attempt to liberate India from British rule.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Subhas Chandra Bose had earlier formed the "Free India Legion" (Indische Legion) with Indian prisoners of war in Germany in 1941-42, a separate initiative from the INA.

 

NOTE

 

• Germany (Option 2): This is where Bose formed the Free India Legion, not the Indian National Army.

 

• London (Option 3): Not associated with the formation of the INA.

 

• Japan (Option 4): While the INA was supported by Japan, it was formed in Singapore, not in Japan itself.

question:
Match the following neighbouring countries with their official languages correctly.

Country name — Official Languages

1. Afghanistan — a. Dzongkha

2. Bhutan — b. Burmese

3. Pakistan — c. Dari

4. Myanmar — d. Urdu
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1-c, 2-a, 3-d, 4-b.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct matches are: Afghanistan - Dari, Bhutan - Dzongkha, Pakistan - Urdu, and Myanmar - Burmese. (पड़ोसी देश और उनकी राजभाषा)

 

• Afghanistan's official languages are Dari (Afghan Persian) and Pashto; Dari is widely used in administration and as a lingua franca.

 

• Bhutan's official language is Dzongkha, spoken predominantly in the western regions of the country.

 

• Pakistan's official languages are Urdu and English, with Urdu serving as the national language, while Myanmar's official language is Burmese (Myanmar language).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other South Asian neighbours of India include Nepal (official language: Nepali), Sri Lanka (Sinhala and Tamil), and Bangladesh (Bengali).

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 3 and 4: These are incorrect because each mismatches at least one country with the wrong official language — for instance, pairing Bhutan with Burmese instead of Dzongkha, or Pakistan with Dari/Burmese instead of Urdu.

question: Which Article in the fundamental duty applies, when a construction worker takes his 8-year son to the site rather than sending him to school?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 51A (k).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 51A(k) of the Indian Constitution imposes a fundamental duty on every parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child, or ward, between the ages of 6 and 14 years. (मौलिक कर्तव्य — अनुच्छेद 51A(k), शिक्षा का अवसर)

 

• This clause was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, the same amendment that inserted Article 21A, making free and compulsory education a fundamental right for children aged 6-14 years.

 

• In the scenario described, the construction worker taking his 8-year-old son to the worksite instead of school violates this duty under Article 51A(k).

 

• The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 operationalises Article 21A, giving legal effect to this constitutional mandate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution via the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, and are listed under Article 51A.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 51A (h) (Option 1): This duty relates to developing scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.

 

• Article 51A (j) (Option 3): This duty relates to striving towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity.

 

• Article 51A (i) (Option 4): This duty relates to safeguarding public property and abjuring violence.

question: Exfoliation is a form of _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is physical weathering.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Exfoliation is a type of physical (mechanical) weathering in which outer layers or shells of rock peel off or flake away from the parent rock mass, typically due to temperature changes. (अपशल्कन — भौतिक अपक्षय)

 

• It occurs mainly due to insolation (differential heating and cooling), causing the outer layer of rock to expand and contract at a different rate than the interior, leading to the peeling off of curved sheets or shells of rock.

 

• It is commonly observed in hot desert regions with large diurnal temperature ranges, and results in characteristic rounded, dome-shaped landforms known as exfoliation domes (e.g., in granite terrains).

 

• Since exfoliation involves purely mechanical disintegration of rock without any change in its chemical composition, it is classified under physical weathering, unlike processes such as oxidation or carbonation, which fall under chemical weathering.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other forms of physical weathering include frost wedging (freeze-thaw action), salt weathering, and block disintegration.

 

NOTE

 

• Chemical weathering (Option 2): Involves processes like oxidation, carbonation, hydrolysis and solution, which alter the chemical composition of rocks — unlike exfoliation.

 

• Mass wasting (Option 3): Refers to the downslope movement of rock and soil material under gravity (e.g., landslides, soil creep), distinct from in-situ weathering processes like exfoliation.

 

• Biochemical weathering (Option 4): Involves the combined chemical and biological action of organisms (e.g., root wedging combined with chemical secretions), which is different from the purely physical process of exfoliation.

question: Which Bill was passed by the Parliament, in July 2021, to help in the availability of working capital for the micro, small and medium enterprises sector?
option_4: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Bill, 2021
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Factoring Regulation (Amendment) Bill, 2021.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Factoring Regulation (Amendment) Bill, 2021 was passed by the Parliament of India in July 2021 to widen the scope of entities that can engage in factoring business, thereby improving the availability of working capital for the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) sector. (फैक्टरिंग विनियमन संशोधन विधेयक, 2021 — MSME को कार्यशील पूंजी)

 

• The Bill amended the Factoring Regulation Act, 2011, expanding the definition of "receivables" and permitting a wider range of Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) to undertake factoring business, not just NBFC-Factors.

 

• "Factoring" refers to a financial arrangement in which a business sells its accounts receivable (invoices) to a third party (a "factor") at a discount, to obtain immediate working capital.

 

• The move was aimed at addressing the chronic problem of delayed payments to MSMEs, thereby easing liquidity constraints.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) is a related electronic platform in India that facilitates the financing/discounting of MSME trade receivables through multiple financiers.

 

NOTE

 

• The Essential Commodities (Amendment) Bill, 2020 (Option 1): This aimed to deregulate commodities like cereals, pulses and onions from stock limits, unrelated to MSME working capital via factoring.

 

• The Minerals Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2020 (Option 2): This related to reforms in the mining sector, unrelated to MSME working capital.

 

• The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Bill, 2021 (Option 4): This introduced a pre-packaged insolvency resolution process (PPIRP) for MSMEs, a different mechanism from factoring-based working capital financing.

question: Identify the structural formula for magnesium hydroxide.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mg(OH)2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Magnesium hydroxide has the chemical formula Mg(OH)2, formed from one magnesium ion (Mg²⁺) and two hydroxide ions (OH⁻), balancing the +2 charge of magnesium with two -1 charged hydroxide ions. (मैग्नीशियम हाइड्रॉक्साइड — Mg(OH)₂)

 

• It is a white, poorly water-soluble solid, commonly known as "milk of magnesia" when in suspension form, and is used as an antacid and laxative.

 

• Magnesium hydroxide is also used as a flame retardant in plastics and as a component in water treatment processes for pH neutralisation and removal of heavy metals.

 

• It can be produced by reacting magnesium oxide (MgO) with water, or by precipitating it from seawater or brine using calcium hydroxide (lime).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• On heating (calcination), magnesium hydroxide decomposes to give magnesium oxide (MgO) and water, a reaction used industrially to produce MgO.

 

NOTE

 

• MgOH (Option 1): This formula is chemically invalid/imbalanced — it does not correctly represent the compound formed by Mg²⁺ and OH⁻ ions.

 

• MgO2 (Option 2): This would represent magnesium peroxide, a different compound from magnesium hydroxide.

 

• Mg2H2 (Option 3): This is not a valid or recognised chemical formula for any known magnesium compound.
